name: Street Custom 'Angry Mary' Aerosol Flamethrower
description: The simplest possible flamethrower: a can of commercial aerosol product — hairspray, lubricant, insecticide — duct-taped to a piezoelectric igniter salvaged from a kitchen lighter. The flame produced is a 1-2 meter cone of burning aerosol propellant that lasts until the can is empty, typically 15-30 seconds of continuous fire. The Angry Mary is not sophisticated, not reliable, and not safe for the operator, but it costs almost nothing, requires no skill to build, and will absolutely set things on fire. It is the weapon of absolute desperation and has been in continuous use in GLMZ's lowest tiers for as long as anyone can remember.
specifications:
flame range: 1-2 meters
fuel: Commercial aerosol can
burn duration: 15-30 seconds per can
ignition: Piezoelectric lighter element
construction time: Under 1 minute
weight: 0.3-0.5 kg
operator risk: High — can rupture, blowback, and burn injuries common
cost: Φ5-15 total
story_hooks: A coordinated arson attack using hundreds of Angry Mary devices hit a corporate facility in Tier 2 — the sheer number suggests organized distribution of a weapon anyone can build.
A survival instructor in Tier 1 has been teaching children to build Angry Marys as self-defense tools — the ethics are horrifying but the threat is real and the children are surviving.

physical_description.visual_profile: A crude, brutally functional contraption: a standard commercial aerosol can wrapped in multiple layers of gray duct tape, with a salvaged piezoelectric igniter rig bolted or taped to the nozzle area. Looks simultaneously pathetic and menacing — the aesthetic of desperation weaponized.
physical_description.dimensions: 18-22 cm length (with igniter assembly), 6-7 cm diameter at can body, igniter housing adds 3-4 cm forward of nozzle
physical_description.weight_description: Light and awkwardly balanced — the full can feels deceptively substantial until ignited, then becomes increasingly lighter as fuel depletes. Grip-heavy forward, making sustained aiming difficult.
physical_description.primary_material: Aluminum aerosol can (inner), duct tape (outer wrapping), salvaged lighter components (igniter — typically brass or cheap steel), wire or bracket adhesive
physical_description.finish: Matte gray duct tape, worn and peeling in places from handling and heat stress. Visible aluminum showing through rips. Igniter components show tarnish and soot from testing or use. Nozzle may be blackened from flame blow-back.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray (duct tape dominant), dull aluminum showing through tears, dark brass/steel igniter hardware, occasional rust-orange corrosion on metal components
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured roughness of duct tape — sticky, slightly tacky, prone to degrading from heat and friction. Poor ergonomics; no deliberate grip design. Igniter trigger area is bare wire or cheap plastic, uncomfortable and liable to slip.
distinctive_features: Visible duct tape layering, some peeling or bubbling
Crude wire framework or bracket holding igniter to can
Scorched and blackened nozzle tip with carbon buildup
Small piezo igniter button, often hastily soldered or glued in place
Hairline cracks in duct tape from previous ignition heat
Possible manufacturer label partially visible under tape (hairspray, WD-40, bug killer, etc.)
Rough solder joints or epoxy blobs where igniter wiring connects
Scorch marks and soot staining around the flame exit point
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Original aerosol can label barely visible under duct tape (brand varies: generic spray adhesive, off-brand lubricant, discount hairspray). 'Street Custom' is purely an unofficial street-tier designation; no legitimate maker's mark exists. Possible handwritten initials or gang tags scratched into tape.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily worn and battle-scarred. Duct tape is dingy, cracked, and peeling. Soot and burn residue around nozzle. The device is perpetually on the edge of mechanical failure — igniter may be unreliable, tape may be partially melted, nozzle may be clogged with propellant residue. Each use risks catastrophic failure (can rupture, igniter misfire, backflash). Field units show tape repairs over tape repairs.
